title: How to Stop Overthinking (5 Tricks That Actually Work)

scenes.narration: It's late, and your brain is replaying that one moment for the fiftieth time.
Overthinking feels productive. Like if you just think hard enough, you'll finally solve it.
But you're not solving anything. You're spinning. Same thought, new lap.
Here are five ways to actually break the loop, backed by psychology, not motivation fluff.
One. Catch it in the act.
Your brain can't spiral and observe itself at the same time.
So the moment you notice it, just say: I'm overthinking again.
Don't judge yourself for it. Label it like a weather report. Ah, overthinking.
That tiny act hands control from your panicked brain back to your calm one.
Two. The ten-ten-ten rule.
Ask yourself: will this matter in ten days? Ten months? Ten years?
Almost everything we agonize over fails the ten-month test.
Overthinking shrinks your whole world down to one moment. This zooms the camera back out.
And if it truly does matter, good. That's your signal to act, not to spiral.
Three. Move to break the loop.
Overthinking lives in your head. The fastest way out is through your body.
Stand up. Walk. Do one tiny piece of the thing you're avoiding.
Wash one dish. Write one sentence. It tells your brain: we're moving now.
Anxiety is just energy with nowhere to go. Action finally gives it somewhere.
Four. You are not your thoughts.
A thought is not a fact. It's just a thought, passing through.
Picture each worry as a cloud drifting across the sky. You are the sky, not the cloud.
Thoughts feel urgent, and they feel true. They are very often neither.
You don't have to grab every single one. Just let it drift past.
Five. Set a decision deadline.
Most overthinking is really just the fear of choosing wrong.
So give the decision a timer. Five minutes. Then commit, and move.
You can almost always adjust later. You can't adjust a choice you never made.
A good decision today beats a perfect one that never comes.
You can't stop thoughts from showing up. That was never the goal.
The goal is to stop feeding them. Notice. Zoom out. Move. Let go. Decide.
Your mind is a tool. And tonight, you're the one holding it.
